newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Spain backs Argentine bid for rich club membership.
newsitem.headline: Spain backs Argentine bid for rich club membership.

text.p: Spanish Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar on Tuesday promised his support for Argentina's bid to join the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), the Paris-based club of rich nations.

"There will probably be technical problems and obstacles to overcome, and possibly political ones, but I believe Argentina's aspirations to join the OECD are well-founded," Aznar said on the last day of a three-day visit to Argentina.
Argentina is a member of G24, which represents developing countries in international monetary negotiations, but has been lobbying hard for membership of the OECD.

President Carlos Menem recently asked visiting French President Jacques Chirac to intercede on Argentina's behalf. Menem said last month Argentina deserved to join because its economic reforms had become "an example for other countries that are lagging behind" in liberalisation and deregulation.

Since Peronist leader Menem came to power in 1989, the country has overcome hyperinflation and economic chaos to become a zero-inflation economy with sustained growth. His enthusiasm for wholesale privatisation has even led Menem to decree the sale of the state post office.
But the country also suffers from high unemployment of more than 17 percent.
Aznar also said Spain and Argentina, key trading partners, would support each others' bids to join the United Nations' Security Council as non-permanent members, Argentina by 1999 and Spain by 2003.

Both countries' armed forces participate in U.N. peacekeeping missions, and Menem has U.N. backing for his "White Helmets" initiative -- multinational groups giving emergency help for areas hit by war or natural disaster or in the grip of starvation and poverty.
